context:
Item-specific guardrails: no external AI endpoints; no gate lifted without validation.

Shared SereneDB guardrails: worktree-only repository writes with make agent-write-preflight; explicit-path staging, never git add -A; commit identity check, no attribution trailers; uv only, no new dependency; lazy psycopg import; no credentials in Git, logs, fixtures, or tracker; Mocker never in CI and its timings never published; pin by digest or exact version and record version(); announce long runs and never commit raw logs; code-skill self-review then make pr-preflight and make pr-open, no auto-merge without make pr-ready; durable artifacts carry no tracker IDs or session narrative; stop and report on failed gates, unverified behavior, or unapproved host changes.
description:
SereneDB's main differentiator is search: BM25 full-text and IVF vector search through inverted indexes (`CREATE INDEX ... USING inverted`, the `@@` operator, `<=>` distance). Evaluate BenchBox's vector_search benchmark (and any full-text workload) on SereneDB with native index DDL and query rewrites.

Tasks:
1. Map the vector_search benchmark's DDL and queries to SereneDB syntax (FLOAT[N] columns, an inverted index with ivf, `<=>` ranking).
2. Register the required schema_emit, query_source, or query_adapter rules in sql_compat.
3. Validate recall and result equivalence against the existing reference platform for that benchmark.
4. Lift the vector_search gate only after validation passes.

Decision gates:
- G1 Start only with explicit user priority.
- G2 Approximate-search results need a documented recall tolerance. If the benchmark has no recall contract, stop and ask.
- G3 AI functions (`ai_embed`) call external model endpoints. Never use them in benchmarks without explicit approval.
